Kabam Robotics plans November 20 shutdown after six years

Customers have reportedly been notified as executives consider an AI-focused direction; arrangements for deployed robots remain to be clarified.

VnExpress International ↗23 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Customers notified ahead of closure

VnExpress, citing The Business Times, reports that Singapore’s Kabam Robotics emailed customers about a November 20 shutdown and asked them to resolve outstanding matters beforehand. Founded under Patec in 2020, Kabam merged with Cognicept Systems in 2022.

Deployments did not remove business pressure

Its patrol, surveillance and inspection robots served customers including Changi Airport Group, Certis and Aetos. The report cites over 150 deployments as of 2023, not a current count. Patec attributed the decision to production costs and market conditions despite industry awards.

Staff and service arrangements remain open

A co-founder confirmed closure to Lianhe Zaobao and discussed shifting from hardware toward AI. A new company and some staff transfers were still under discussion. The affected workforce count and support arrangements for installed robots remain unclear.
